Assembly membership = the three parcels currently deeded to J5 LLC (the disclosed developer of record; City of Piqua project page piquaoh.gov/1673). Two of the three (N44-101834, N44-101846) carry the same 2025-12-24 conveyance for $62,234,725; N44-101770 has no sale date/amount on the layer (acquired separately or unposted) — [open], verify against the recorder deed.

Class code is 101 ('cash-grain / general farm') on all three: the tract is still assessed AGRICULTURAL (recently-purchased farmland, not yet reclassified) — a CAUV flag (has_cauv) rides on each. This is the pre-construction assessment, not the data-center use.

split_lineage is the auditor SMDA# split/merge note (all three trace to the M40-WA022 Washington-Twp parent-parcel series); it is the trail that ties the assemblage together and was how the campus parcels were identified.

ACREAGE RECONCILIATION (resolves the issue's ~1,026 vs ~1,200 ac question — the auditor pull shows these are NESTED SCOPES, not a missing fourth parcel): (a) the J5-owned data-center campus = 607.842 ac [verified, this file]; (b) an adjacent 93.105-ac parcel (N44-101772, 2332 W Farrington Rd) is held by 'J3 DEVELOPMENT LLC' — SAME M40-WA022 split lineage, different mailing (Cincinnati, not J5's Columbus), so common control is [inference] only; it is a lead, NOT committed here (see README / data-centers.md); (c) the full M40-WA022 split-parent series = 7 parcels / 963.794 ac, of which 262.847 ac stays farm-owned in Washington Twp (Hines, Holfinger x2) [verified lineage]; (d) the City page's ~1,026-ac and ~1,200-ac figures describe the cumulative ANNEXATION record (2022-2025) and the whole I-75 Exit 78 Business & Industrial Park respectively — both LARGER scopes than the developer-owned campus. The campus (owner of record) is ~608 ac, not 1,026 or 1,200.
